title: The Share of Premium Returned on a Release of Cover
content:
The share of the premium returned when cover under the Travel Protection Plans is given up turns on how
long after issue the cover is released and on whether any claim stands filed on the policy.

## The free-look period each plan carries

| Plan | Free-look period (days) |
|---|---|
| Trip Basics Essential | 10 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 10 |
| TripGuard Plus | 14 |
| TripGuard Premier | 14 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 15 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 15 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 21 |

## The three readings

1. Where cover is given up more than the plan's free-look period after the day the certificate was issued and no
   claim stands filed on the policy, the share returned is the plan's mid-term share.
2. Where a claim stands filed on the policy, nothing is returned.
3. In every other case the share returned is the plan's free-look share.

The second reading answers wherever a claim stands filed, whether the release falls inside the plan's free-look
period or beyond it. The first reading turns on the day count exceeding the plan's period: a release exactly on
the last day of that period has not passed it, and the third reading answers instead.

## Points of judgement

On a TripGuard Plus policy, whose free-look period is 14 days, cover released 14 days after the day the
certificate was issued is not more than the period, and the share returned is the plan's free-look share; cover
released on the 15th day is more than the period, and where no claim stands filed the share returned is the
plan's mid-term share. On an Annual Multi-Trip Executive policy the same turn comes at 21 days, and on a Trip
Basics Essential policy at 10. Where a claim stands filed on any of them, nothing is returned however few days
have passed.
